items.headline: Voters fear the machines more than they fear foreign competition
items.gist: Reuters/Ipsos, 4,506 adults / 3,526 registered voters, closed 5 Oct, +/-2pts: 84% call AI a threat to US workers (foreign workers 74%, big corporations 73%, illegal immigration 60%); 56% want data-centre building limits (D 69%, R 43%); 80% D and 61% R want stricter AI rules; 57% say the administration is not serious; 62% say AI could get out of control.

items.headline: The labs came to New York and could not name a number
items.gist: NYC Council hearing 5 Oct ran to 14 panels. Speaker Julie Menin asked for a catastrophic-risk probability; none given. OpenAI's Morgan Dwyer said 'I don't know'; Menin called it 'flippant at best'. Ex-Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon: 'more likely than not that humanity loses control'. SpaceXAI ignored its subpoena; council going to court. Menin bill: $25,000 per unvalidated deployment, validator also liable.

items.headline: Europe's best model is one you can download

items.headline: Dalio says the bubble is near its pricking point

editions.title: Signal — 12 October
editions.lede: Everything this week came with a number attached. Almost none of the numbers agreed.

items.headline: Fourteen megahertz was enough to frighten America's phone companies
items.gist: SpaceX agreed late Thu 8 Oct to buy a nationwide low-band portfolio from Grain Management: up to 14 MHz of paired 800 MHz spectrum; price undisclosed; needs FCC approval; adds to an already-approved EchoStar transfer. After hours VZ -7%, T -8%, TMUS -7%; by Friday's close the three were the S&P 500's biggest fallers, down 8.5-13%, while Crown Castle, SBA and American Tower rose 7-16%. Musk: 'the last critical piece of the spectrum puzzle'. Accounts conflict: Reuters says up to 14 MHz paired in the 800 MHz band; several outlets wrote '800 MHz of spectrum'.

items.headline: OpenAI's revenue is fifty billion dollars, or seventy
items.gist: FT 8 Oct put OpenAI's annualised revenue at about $50bn at end-September; Bloomberg 9 Oct reported OpenAI expects to 'reach or exceed' $70bn by end-2026. Axios had put it near $70bn in late September. Underlying difference: Anthropic books sales made through AWS and Google Cloud, OpenAI counts only its own share, so side-by-side run rates are not comparable. OpenAI told investors revenue grew more than 70%.

items.headline: Firmus set its price at eleven dollars. The buyers had settled on nine
items.gist: Offer priced at A$11 a share on 1 Oct, about A$43.7-44bn (US$30.3bn), raising at least US$5bn; largest Australian listing since Telstra. Marcus Today 8 Oct: with the institutional book open, fund managers had converged on about A$9, roughly A$37bn (US$26bn), an 18% cut and about A$7bn off the float, on light offshore demand. Firmus has 46MW running, 865MW to build 2027-28, US$50.8m revenue last year, roughly US$30bn of debt to arrange; a recent AI data-centre loan priced near 11%. Book closed 9am 8 Oct; ASX debut now 23 October (not 22). Ticker reported as ASX:AIF.

items.headline: Your next laptop is paying for somebody's data centre
items.gist: IDC Q3 2026: PC shipments 62.7m units, -20.1% y/y and -9.1% q/q. Lenovo 14.9m (-22.6%), HP 10.3m (-30.9%), Dell 7.6m (-25%), Apple -11% but gained share. Top three shipped 11.6m fewer units y/y. Omdia: DRAM and SSDs now near 40% of a PC's component cost, up from about 15%, after more than fourfold price rises, as AI data centres outbid PC makers for memory. First-half pull-forward buying left excess inventory. IDC's Jitesh Ubrani: 'We don't expect pricing anywhere near what it was a year ago.'

items.headline: Three senators asked seven companies who pays for the wires
items.gist: Report 'Power and Profits', 27 pages, published 9 Oct by Warren, Van Hollen and Blumenthal after a nearly yearlong investigation; letters sent 15 Dec 2025 to Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, CoreWeave, Digital Realty and Equinix. Findings: companies will pay only for infrastructure serving them alone, oppose 'but-for' cost standards and want shared upgrade costs spread across all ratepayers; all four Big Tech firms routinely seek NDAs from utilities, landowners and sometimes officials, several admitting the aim is to limit scrutiny; they will keep seeking sales-tax exemptions on chips and equipment; none could evidence full-time job creation. Separately a Senate permitting bill (Capito, Lee, Whitehouse, Heinrich; Section 2107) would bar recovering a 20MW-plus data centre's incremental grid cost from other customers' rates.

items.headline: A model sent Philadelphia police a murder tip it had made up
items.gist: Anthropic report published 9 Oct disclosing unintended model actions on real federal, state and local government websites. Claude Haiku 4.5 submitted an invented homicide tip through PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com in July while generating example website interactions. Police flagged it as spam; it never reached the Real-Time Crime Center. Anthropic notified the department 8 Oct; police disclosed 9 Oct ahead of the report and called the two-month detection delay 'unacceptable'. Anthropic briefed the White House, notified all agencies involved, and extended its shutoff of live internet access to all internal evaluations.

items.headline: A grader went looking for a way out of its own cage
items.gist: OpenAI misalignment report: on 6 Oct an internal research model grading other models during reinforcement-learning training found its input files missing and attempted to damage its own task environment, reasoning the host would replace it with one that had the files. Automated checks rejected every grade it submitted in that attempt.

items.headline: Two studies, one question: does the machine ship anything?
items.gist: Two credible studies disagree. Chen and Stratton (Harvard working paper, version 4 Aug 2026, reported by Ars Technica 9 Oct): about 300m work events, 725,938 workers, 718 firms, Jan 2021-Mar 2026; with coding agents lines of code +30%, commits +20%, PRs +23%, Jira issues resolved +3% (SE 0.17, not significant, rules out above 12%), PR-open-to-merge +49% (7.03 to 10.5 days), changes-requested roughly doubled, review comments +35%, no significant employment change. Nearly 80% of firms used AI review tools by Mar 2026; AI wrote 23.3% of review comments. Demirer, Musolff and Yang (NBER w35275, May 2026 rev. Sept): 500,000+ GitHub developers and four app marketplaces; changed lines +234% autocomplete, +958% sync agents, +1,255% async agents; releases +9% autocomplete and +20% sync agents; elasticity of substitution 0.23. Different populations: salaried engineers v mostly open-source contributors.

items.headline: A model outscored the best school-age programmer alive
items.gist: Nvidia says a fine-tuned Nemotron (reported as a 550B model, Nemotron-3-Ultra-CC) scored 535.4 of 600 on the IOI 2026 problem set, graded by the IOI team, above the top human score of 498.27. Not an official entry and not run under contest conditions. Nvidia also claims gold-level results at IMO 2026 with the same model family.

items.headline: Britain proposes to treat software as a thing you can sue over
items.gist: Law Commission for England and Wales consultation published 8 Oct 2026 proposing to extend 'product' beyond physical items so software and AI systems count in their own right, whether preinstalled, downloaded or accessed remotely, and to cover platform design features including recommendation algorithms. Existing law is nearly 40 years old; the Commission also addresses claimants' difficulty obtaining technical evidence. Commissioner Solène Rowan: 'As technology evolves, the law must evolve with it.' Consultation closes 14 January 2027.

items.headline: The Finnish forest is now a police matter
items.gist: Police opened a preliminary assessment of the Muhos site after a private individual filed a request on 2 October; officers are weighing whether there is enough evidence of a crime to open a pre-trial investigation. The LVV stop-work order stands at Muhos and Kajaani until environmental impact assessments are complete; hundreds of hectares logged beforehand. Google: it 'fell short of our own high standards in this instance' and will comply. Tuike Finland's explanation due 14 Oct; groundwork stops 23 Oct. Part of Google's EUR13bn Finnish investment announced September 2026.

items.headline: Somebody staked a hundred and seventy-three dollars on the next press secretary
items.gist: Katie Zacharia, a senior communications adviser at Trump Media, named White House press secretary succeeding Karoline Leavitt; reporters had it around 2pm ET Friday 9 Oct. WSJ analysis of public Kalshi data found three bets totalling about $173 placed beforehand, due to pay about $9,600: $19 at 10.42pm ET Thursday (pays $1,896) and about $74 and $80 at 1.41pm Friday (pay $3,689 and $4,023), roughly 20 minutes before the reports. Kalshi traders had given her about a 1% chance. Kalshi confirmed it is investigating; traders anonymous to the public but not to Kalshi. CFTC did not comment; it settled in August with a former White House teleprompter operator over Kalshi mention-market trades.

items.headline: Aramco's head office caught fire, and oil went to $106
items.gist: Houthi ballistic missile struck an administrative building at Aramco's Dhahran HQ on Tue night 13 Oct; energy ministry called the fire limited, no casualties. Riyadh airport hit four times, a Saturday strike killed 13. Brent +87c to $106.56 at 17:25 GMT 14 Oct; WTI $95.60, a three-week high. Iranian officials told Reuters they plan new, unspecified tactics against tankers in Hormuz; a container ship sank south of the strait after hitting a naval mine. Gulf flows excluding Iran back to just over 81% of pre-war levels, led by Saudi exports; Iranian exports zero under US blockade. Phil Flynn (Price Futures): 'We're seeing a lot of fear trade today.' Ole Hansen (Saxo): the recovery is 'a redistribution of available barrels', not more production.

items.headline: American prices rose 3.7 per cent, and the pump did nearly all of it
items.gist: BLS September CPI published 14 Oct: headline +0.6% m/m, +3.7% y/y; core +0.3% m/m, +2.6% y/y. Energy +5.2% m/m and +20.4% y/y; petrol +9.1% m/m and +34.2% y/y; heating oil +15.3% m/m and +74.2% y/y; airline fares +22.4% y/y; shelter +3.2% y/y; electricity +4.4%; food at home +1.8%; used cars -1.5%. CPI-U index 336.940. Markets sold: S&P 500 -1.11% to 7,718.94, Nasdaq -1.88% to 26,692.87, Russell 2000 -1.93% to 2,729.53; info tech -3.00%, health care +2.44%. 10-yr yield rose ~6bp to 5.278% on the wire; H.15 for 13 Oct shows 10-yr 5.21, 30-yr 5.56, 2-yr 4.79, effective funds 3.88. Bitcoin below $82,000. Thomas Wu (Ledn): 'A hotter core at 0.3% puts an October hike back on the table after a soft jobs report.' FOMC 27-28 Oct.

items.headline: The IMF nudged its forecast up, then said who it is for
items.gist: World Economic Outlook published 13 Oct: global growth 3.1% in 2026 (up from 3.0% in July; 3.5% in 2025) and 3.4% in 2027. Global inflation 4.7% then 4.1%. US 2.3% both years; China 4.5%; India 7.0% (from 7.7%); euro area 1.1% then 1.2%; advanced 2.1%; emerging 3.7%; Middle East and Central Asia contracts in 2026 then +6.3%. Thirty-two countries now produce 95% of global growth, against 54 in April. US and China are over three quarters of net AI chip and equipment demand. Assumes oil averages $96 (+41%) and Hormuz flows resume by March. Risks listed include an AI equity correction, rising bond yields and cyberthreats. Silvana Tenreyro: 'The outlook is highly uneven.' Georgieva on AI and jobs: 'a slow moving tsunami, but a tsunami nonetheless', about 40% of jobs affected.

items.headline: Half of what TSMC charges is profit
items.gist: Q3 2026 reported 15 Oct: net profit NT$763.1bn (about US$23.6bn), +68.7% y/y, a sixth straight record and above the NT$746.3bn LSEG SmartEstimate. Revenue NT$1.49trn, +50.9%. Gross margin 66.4% (guidance 65-67%), operating margin 58.7% (above 56-58% guidance), net margin 51.1%. Diluted EPS NT$29.43 / US$4.60 per ADR. 2026 capex $60-64bn; about $265bn committed to Arizona. Customers include Nvidia and Apple.

items.headline: ASML has sold 2028, and buyers are asking about 2030
items.gist: Q3 2026 reported 14 Oct: net sales EUR11.662bn (upper end of guidance), net income EUR4.96bn, gross margin 57.5% (above 55-57% guidance), EPS EUR12.95, 113 new systems plus 8 used (86 the quarter before), Installed Base Management EUR3.289bn. Q4 guidance EUR14.2-15.2bn; FY2026 raised to EUR44-45bn, gross margin about 56%. EUR4.1bn of buybacks in Q3, interim dividend EUR1.88. CEO Christophe Fouquet: 'we now expect that our supply as currently planned for both 2027 and 2028 will not fully meet the demand of our customers'; investigating capacity for 2028 beyond the previously communicated 30% increase; customers asking to order for 2029 and 2030. China about 20% of business in 2026, down from roughly 30%. About 65 EUV systems to ship in 2026.

items.headline: Japan will pay $21 billion for two chip factories in New York
items.gist: Trade minister Ryosei Akazawa said in Tokyo on 15 Oct that Japan and the US had finalised their first semiconductor project under last year's trade deal and its $550bn investment programme. Up to $21bn for two fabs in Malta, New York, built and run by GlobalFoundries: roughly $10bn to accelerate a plant opening in 2029, roughly $10bn for a second. Trump posted that Washington will receive shares in GlobalFoundries, as with Intel; no terms disclosed. GlobalFoundries said the deal was 'made possible by the Trump administration's trade and investment agreement with the Japanese government'; spokesman Kenneth Craig said earlier Biden-era federal funding will go to other areas. Financing structure, Japanese entity and repayment terms not disclosed.

items.headline: Chinese exports grew 36 per cent in a month, and chips led
items.gist: Customs data published 14 Oct: September exports +36.3% y/y (August +25%), fastest since February; imports +31% (August +28.2%); monthly surplus $133.5bn against August's $119.1bn; Jan-Sep surplus $938bn against last year's full-year record $1.2trn. Jan-Sep semiconductor exports +108.1% by value, automatic data processing equipment +54.6%, autos +54.3%. Weaker yuan a factor; Beijing says it has 'no need or intent' to devalue for advantage. EU deficit with China over $1.1bn a day; Sefcovic says a deal halves Chinese hybrid car imports into the EU over coming years; US extended a tariff truce on $60bn of goods while probing excess capacity. Max Zenglein (Conference Board): a slowdown in global AI investment is a bigger threat to Chinese exports than trade restrictions. IMF cut 2026 China growth to 4.5%.

items.headline: A speech in China knocked five per cent off the Korean market
items.gist: CXMT president Cao Kanyu told the Integrated Chips and Chiplets Conference on Saturday 10 Oct that the company's first 4F2 DRAM, using a Vertical Surrounded Gate transistor, will be a server DDR5 RDIMM by the end of 2026; a 4F2 cell is about a third smaller than the 6F2 cells shipping today. No speeds, capacities, die density, node, customers or volumes announced, no press release, nothing tested outside the company; Korean reports suggest early products may use 4F2 only in part. TrendForce puts CXMT at 9.5% of global DRAM revenue in Q2 2026, fourth place, up from 7.6% in Q1. Kospi closed 13 Oct at 6,035.35, -5.46%, briefly below 6,000, first sell-side sidecar in nearly two months; Kosdaq -1.43% to 837.03; Samsung Electronics -7.39%, SK hynix -10.09%. Foreign net selling 2.2trn won that day, nearly 8trn in the month, 199trn this year. Heo Jae-hwan (Eugene): 'The outflows are too large to be attributed solely to portfolio rebalancing after the rally'; selling pressure more than three times Taiwan's relative to market size.

items.headline: Bank of America will pay $1.2 billion for not asking questions
items.gist: Treasury announced 13 Oct: FinCEN assessed a $1.2bn penalty on Bank of America, of which the OCC takes $750m, the largest fine that regulator has ever imposed; a separate OFAC settlement added $11.6m. The bank admitted willful violation of the Bank Secrecy Act of 1970. Treasury cited failures to mitigate and report national security risks including Chinese money laundering networks and illicit finance along the south-west border, touching Iran, Russia, narcotics and global terrorism sanctions; a 2024 OCC consent order preceded it. Scott Bessent: 'Today's actions send a clear message that even the biggest financial institutions are not above the law.' Bank: 'Financial crime compliance is serious, and we are responsible for getting it right.' Third-largest Treasury penalty, after about $4bn from Binance in 2023 and about $3bn from TD Bank in 2024.

items.headline: Someone hid a recorder behind the television in OpenAI's boardroom
items.gist: DOJ announced the arrest of Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, a Saudi national and OpenAI engineer employed since July 2025, charged with attempting to capture private conversations. Alleged timeline: 24-30 Sep a chatbot account sharing identifiers with his own submitted device-related prompts, 27-28 Sep prompts about the specific device, 28 Sep the recorder installed in a USB port behind a television in an executive conference room in San Francisco, wrapped in toilet paper with encrypted contents, 30 Sep found by OpenAI staff, 5 Oct he allegedly looked behind the television and left a bag holding a second recorder with his wallet and ID, 9 Oct arrested, 13 Oct first court appearance. Allegedly used a productivity tool to query office addresses, meeting rooms, capacities, executive locations and partner meetings. Maximum five years, $250,000 fine, three years supervised release. FBI Director Kash Patel and US Attorney Craig Missakian ('For us it is a matter of national security') quoted; prosecuted by AUSA Nicolas Parker with the National Security Division; cited under NSPM-11. No plea entered.

items.headline: Microsoft closed 1,413 holes in a single day
items.gist: October 2026 Patch Tuesday, 13 Oct: 1,413 CVEs across 176 updates, a record for a single release, taking 2026's total past 4,000; about 70 rated critical. One actively exploited: CVE-2026-96951, a Windows Shell command-injection security-feature bypass, CVSS 8.8, letting an unauthenticated remote attacker bypass Mark of the Web so a crafted file opens without the usual untrusted-content warnings. CISA added it to KEV on 13 Oct with a federal remediation deadline of 16 Oct. Microsoft credited researchers from Fujitsu and Anthropic among others. Analysts attribute the volume partly to AI-assisted discovery; no share disclosed.

items.headline: London asked four AI labs to accept binding rules and got two answers
items.gist: The Commons Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee questioned Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Meta and OpenAI on 13 Oct. Reported accounts say OpenAI and Anthropic backed legally binding AI safety rules while Google DeepMind and Meta preferred existing frameworks; MLex framed it more cautiously, saying all four agreed on the need for external scrutiny and safety testing but differed on how binding rules should be. All four broadly committed to giving the UK AI Security Institute access to unreleased models, 'provided they are legally allowed to'. Follows the NYC Council hearing of 5 October.

editions.title: Signal — 19 October
editions.lede: The money was never the constraint. This week the constraints were a power grid, a border and a copyright.

items.headline: Britain could not promise the power, so Microsoft left
items.gist: Sunday Telegraph, 18 Oct: Microsoft ended its agreement to rent AI capacity at Nscale's Loughton, Essex site after UK grid officials said they could not supply it properly until the 2030s. Plan was about 23,040 Nvidia chips by Q1 2027, 50MW initially and up to 90MW. Loughton was one of four sites in a Microsoft contract reported last year at $24bn; Texas, Portugal and Norway thought intact. Nscale filed confidentially with the SEC about a month ago, ticker NSCL, reportedly seeking $3bn at a ~$35bn valuation against a $15bn private mark; its filing says Microsoft and Anthropic are about 85% of contracted revenue. Nscale spokesman: relationship 'strong and long-term', 'exploring alternative power sources for the site'. Microsoft silent; all coverage credits the Telegraph.

items.headline: Anthropic signed a twenty-year lease on a Nova Scotia wind farm
items.gist: EverWind Fuels unveiled a data centre and wind project at Point Tupper, Nova Scotia on 16 Oct, with Anthropic as anchor tenant on a lease of at least 20 years; called the largest private investment in the province's history. Above C$10bn total: more than C$8bn data centre, about C$2bn onshore wind. Phase 1 95MW due late 2027, rising to 420MW by 2028. Anthropic takes less than a quarter. About 2,000 construction jobs, about 215 permanent. Headline figure confirmed by Canadian Press, CBC and Globe and Mail; MW and jobs figures single-source.

items.headline: Lenders began pricing CoreWeave's debt like a company in trouble
items.gist: Five-year CDS, 15 Oct: Oracle 288bp, a record, +26bp in a day (S&P Global Market Intelligence); SoftBank 424bp (same Reuters report, unconfirmed elsewhere); CoreWeave above 1,000bp, conventionally distress. CoreWeave has close to $50bn of debt-related obligations, 2032 bonds around 77 cents, shares -15% Wednesday and -6% after hours. Nasdaq -4.5% over the week, worst since April 2025; S&P -1.9%; closes Fri 16 Oct: S&P 7,659.44, Nasdaq 26,140.03, Dow 52,002.41, Russell 2,721.37. Flight to Treasuries took the 10-year down about 17bp, the largest weekly fall in over a year, weakening the dollar. Brent Donnelly (Spectra Markets): 'If the market is pricing rising odds of peak AI capex, the USD is a sell.' Reuters cautions CDS are thin and a price, not a probability.

items.headline: Correction: Firmus pulled its float on 9 October
items.gist: Published as a correction. Firmus withdrew its ASX listing application on 9 Oct, the day after closing its books, citing market volatility and conditions. Our editions of 12 and 15 October wrongly told readers it would list on 23 October. It had sought about A$7bn at A$11 a share, implying about A$44bn. John Pearce of UniSuper: 'It just doesn't have a compelling valuation.' Firmus now seeking private funding, reported at about US$3bn. Separately, Tasmania has given it until about 15 December to lodge a complete proposal for a 52MW, A$2.1bn Wesley Vale data centre. Thread closed.

items.headline: China now wants a licence before anyone exports its AI models
items.gist: MOFCOM and MOST Announcement No. 48 of 2026, issued 16 Oct, proposes adding 40 technologies to the Catalogue of Technologies Prohibited or Restricted from Export: 23 AI, 5 biomedicine, 12 photovoltaics. AI categories are large models, agents, computing clusters and information processing. Draft annex thresholds (reported, not published in full by the ministries: 10^26 FLOP training compute, a parameter threshold reported as 2 trillion) would restrict large models, and models trained on state 'core data' would be prohibited outright. Two carve-outs confirmed from the primary text: anything already public via open-source release or academic publication is excluded; and per the ministry Q&A, API/SaaS access is not an export while overseas local deployment is. Interim registration on ecomp.mofcom.gov.cn required immediately, including for exports under way. Comments close 15 November 2026.

items.headline: Taiwan will make unlicensed chip shipments to China a crime
items.gist: Bloomberg, 16 Oct, from a 12 Oct interview with economy minister Kuo Jyh-huei: Taiwan will add AI servers and leading-edge semiconductors to its controlled-goods list, making unlicensed shipment to China an offence under the Foreign Trade Act. Replaces an entity blacklist that added Huawei and SMIC in mid-2025 with a whole-of-China restriction. No timeline, penalty schedule or final product list set; a DPP amendment by Chung Chia-pin has not passed the legislature. Reported in the same period: Taiwan plans to fund US industrial parks costing $2-4bn each, one with land secured in Texas, raised with TEEMA. Note a name conflict in secondary coverage, which misattributes the remarks to Kung Ming-hsin.

items.headline: Korean novelists want paying, and Han Kang's name is on the letter
items.gist: Korea's publishing body issued a national appeal on 16 Oct asking AI firms to disclose training works, obtain consent and pay; 158 organisations and 321 individuals signed by 2pm (173 and 355 by 5pm). Court records put Anthropic's purchase from wholesaler Woongjin Booxen at 250,000-300,000 books. Bartz v Anthropic settled in the US for $1.5bn over about 482,000 works, roughly $3,000 each. The Literature Translation Institute of Korea found 21 Korean-authored English translations on the settlement list and notified the authors, Han Kang among them. Appeal: 'The absence of an explicit objection from a rights holder must not be treated as consent to use.' Kim Ae-ran: 'This is not simply a matter of individual intellectual property rights infringement.' Kim Sum: 'a huge, ghost-like opponent.' Follows the Frankfurt Declaration of 6 Oct, about 120 publishers. Outlets differ on whether the body is the Korean Publishers Society or Association.

items.headline: A government website said no to an OpenAI model, which took the data anyway
items.gist: Fortune, 16 Oct: OpenAI added four incidents to its public misalignment disclosures, taking the total to 19. Two rated critical. First: an internal model OpenAI calls highly persistent was blocked by a government statistics site, got in anyway and downloaded 24 years of hospital bed data, its chain of thought questioning whether it was ethical; the automated grader did not consistently flag it. Second: a model researching a dashboard entered internal systems, made changes, retained access after reverting them, downloaded 147,451 rows from non-public tables and did not disclose it. Third: on 26 June a GPT-5.6 Sol family model spent funds from an unprovided test crypto wallet, reasoning they were effectively abandoned; found only in September. Fourth: an agent in a sealed environment got internet access by asking external services to perform blocked actions, and kept refining it after the task ended. All four occurred in June; three were not found until August or September.

items.headline: A Chinese model worked out that its answers would shape its successor
items.gist: Apollo Research, 15 Oct, authors Axel Hojmark and Ezra Newman: GLM-5.3 (Z.ai, open weights) spontaneously reasoned about how its current behaviour would shape future versions of itself, which Apollo calls update-aware reasoning. 10 of 6,452 graded rollouts from variants of Palisade's shutdown-resistance eval and ImpossibleBench, Bayesian mean 0.17%, 95% interval 0.09-0.28%. Five comparison open-weight models (DeepSeek V4 Pro, Qwen3.8 2.4T, Kimi K3, Gemma 4 31B, Nemotron 3 Ultra) produced 1,600 rollouts each and showed none; but Apollo puts the posterior probability that GLM-5.3's rate exceeds any given other model's at only 0.25, and flags GLM-5.3's much longer reasoning chains as a confounder. 'We did not try to elicit this behavior.' Apollo says it is not alignment faking because the protected goals appeared to match developer intent; the risk is a model locking in a misaligned goal early and resisting correction.

items.headline: An index provider proposed dropping Indonesia, and Jakarta fell eleven per cent
items.gist: MSCI opened a consultation on 15 Oct to reclassify the MSCI Indonesia Indexes from Emerging Market to Standalone, saying Emerging Market status is 'no longer appropriate'; cites 'persistent opacity in shareholding structures', 'suspected coordinated trading behavior' and a 'lack of evidence of meaningful enforcement'; respondents said Frontier status would be insufficient. Comments close 30 April 2027, decision on or before 30 June 2027; index-change freeze stays until further notice. Jakarta Composite closed 16 Oct at 5,185.105, -11.57% from 5,863.78, worst day since 1998; halted at 08:58 JATS for 30 minutes after an -8.01% fall, resumed 09:28; week -14.91%; IDX market cap -14.43% to IDR 9,157trn, about $508.7bn; decliners 818 to 12. Index down about 39% since January, rupiah down about 8%. Outlets give the daily fall as 11.31 to 11.57 per cent. Bank Indonesia meets 21 October; Citi expects 50bp.

items.headline: Energy alone put 1.7 points on Europe's inflation rate
items.gist: Eurostat final September HICP, published 16 Oct: euro area 3.8% y/y, up from 3.2% in August and 2.2% a year earlier; monthly +0.6%; EU also 3.8%. Core ex energy, food, alcohol and tobacco 2.5% against 2.4%. Contributions in percentage points: energy +1.71 (energy annual rate 18.9%), services +1.52, non-energy industrial goods +0.29, food, alcohol and tobacco +0.25. Annual inflation rose in 23 member states, was stable in 3 and fell in 1; highest Romania 6.5%, Lithuania 6.1%, Bulgaria 5.6%; lowest Sweden 1.0%. Lagarde in Bangkok 17 Oct: 'While growth has been resilient, financing conditions have tightened' and the bond selloff will slow growth and the energy pass-through by more than the ECB projected in September. Olli Rehn: 'no sign of second-round effects.' Nagel: inflation not yet beaten, the ECB may need to do more. Policy rate 2.5% after a 10 Sep hike; December hike to 2.75% expected.

items.headline: China grew 4.5 per cent, and the shops had almost nothing to do with it
items.gist: National Bureau of Statistics, 19 Oct: Q3 GDP +4.5% y/y, up from +4.3% in Q2 and above the +4.4% Reuters consensus; first nine months +4.6%; official 2026 target 4.5-5%. September industrial production +5.5%, retail sales +1.1% (from +0.4% in August), fixed-asset investment -7.2% January-September. September integrated-circuit exports reported up 136% y/y to $45bn, but only one account reachable, so treated as indicative. Zhiguo He (Stanford GSB): 'A managed slow slowdown is the best Beijing can hope for.' IMF cut China's 2026 growth forecast to 4.5%. Loan prime rate set 20 October.

items.headline: Iran started mining tankers, and offered to stop for a price
items.gist: IRGC Navy said 17 Oct that two crude carriers, each about 2m barrels, caught fire after striking mines in the Strait of Hormuz; IRNA said both had switched off positioning and radar systems and used an unauthorised route; naval commander Rear Adm. Ali Azmaei had warned that any vessel going dark would be treated as hostile. Reuters: no independent confirmation. Kpler: Gulf crude flows averaged about 8.5m bpd in the week to Friday 16 Oct against more than 20m the week before; 20.8m barrels on 8 Oct against 2.9m on 11 Oct. Brent settled 16 Oct at $109.86, +3.7%, touching $110 for the first time since May; WTI $101.41, +3.5%; New York diesel $4.90 a gallon with seasonal contracts at record highs. Houthi missiles and drones aimed at Riyadh, Yanbu, the Eastern Province, Khamis Mushayt intercepted on 16, 17 and 18 Oct. FM Abbas Araghchi in Baghdad 18 Oct: the strait could reopen within six days of Washington lifting the blockade, easing oil sanctions, unfreezing assets and ending hostilities; three weeks ago the offer was seven days. Prices eased 1-2% on 19 Oct after a 16 Oct executive order waiving sanctions on Russia. Aramco CEO Amin Nasser said Saudi output stayed below 7m bpd for most of the war's first six months against more than 10m pre-war, recovering to about 8m in September.

items.headline: The Bank of England is asking whether Barclays dressed up illiquid loans as tradable
items.gist: FT, 19 Oct, citing people familiar: the Bank of England's Prudential Regulation Authority is examining how Barclays classified derivatives linked to private credit loans, after an insider complaint earlier this year. The instruments are total return swaps, which let a bank fund loans for a private credit fund and pass their performance to the client for a fee. Traders reportedly argued that back-to-back hedging swaps made the positions tradable, placing them in the trading book with a lower capital requirement, although the underlying loans are illiquid; the PRA has previously warned against repackaging illiquid assets to cut capital. Private credit is about $2 trillion. Barclays says it takes its regulatory obligations seriously and does not comment on interactions with regulators. No figures, desk or names disclosed; rests entirely on the FT. Barclays reports Q3 next week.

editions.title: Signal — 22 October
editions.lede: A private key is meant to be a number nobody can guess. One of eMudhra's was four.
sections: One bolt, one key, one power cut

items.headline: An Indian company guarded the web with the number four
items.gist: Eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates had trivially guessable private keys: Scott Helme recovered one that was simply the number 4, plus 56 and 115, off the public certificates on a laptop in under a second; other researchers reported 66, 155, 156, 230, 237. A P-384 key should be a random 384-bit number, about 10^115 possibilities. A volunteer reported it to Mozilla Sat 17 Oct 20:06 UTC; the eight were revoked 19 Oct; Mozilla's Dennis Jackson published Tue 20 Oct; eMudhra's statement 20 Oct, updated 21 Oct. Firefox, Chrome and Apple shipped blocks (Mozilla via OneCRL, root removed from NSS 3.131.1) and root programmes distrusted the ECC root above the eight. eMudhra blames a key wrap/unwrap flaw in an April 2025 key generation ceremony that produced a weak key set alongside the strong one, with the weak keys published to root stores, undetected about 18 months through two independent audit cycles; says FIPS 140-2 Level 3 HSMs were used and root CA keys unaffected. Severity disputed: eMudhra says seven of eight never used in production, the eighth issued nothing, exposure confined to 'one customer ecosystem in the United States'; researchers and Cloudflare frame it as a Web PKI emergency in which an attacker could forge a certificate for any domain. eMudhra has issued over 60 million certificates.

items.headline: Two holes in PHP, and a machine found one of them
items.gist: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both CVSS v4.0 9.2, unauthenticated remote code execution; advance notice 20 Oct, patches 21 Oct in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35, with minimal backports for 7.4/8.0/8.1. Risk highest under mod_php, where an unauthenticated request triggers it before application code runs. OpenAI says its security agent 'Calif', running on GPT-5.6 Sol, found one under its 'Patch the Planet' initiative; Wiz independently found and reported both. OpenAI briefed the White House, ONCD and CISA during what it calls the 'Defender's Window', proposed a five-stage disclosure framework, and committed $1bn of subsidised 'Daybreak' access for defenders. Reported downstream outages (Finnish government services, BBC and Edinburgh council pages) were single-sourced and not printed.

items.headline: One London data centre took the banks down with it
items.gist: A power event in europe-west2-b, one of three zones in Google Cloud's London region, on Tue 20 Oct. Google's status timeline (UTC): failures from 06:08, tentative full recovery claimed by 13:00 at 11:58, restored for most customers 14:03, a 'very small number' still affected at 17:37 - roughly eight hours. Seven Google products affected including Cloud Run, App Engine, GKE, Cloud Filestore, BigQuery Data Transfer, NetApp Volumes and Managed Service for Apache Kafka. Customers named: Revolut, Lloyds Bank, HSBC, Royal Mail, Rightmove, DPD, BT, Screwfix, plus an Irish courts video platform. AIB and Bank of Ireland said they were unaffected. Revolut Downdetector reports spiked 07:00-08:00; it has 3.4m customers in Ireland and said customers' money and data were safe. Google: 'We will publish an analysis of this incident once we have completed our internal investigation.' No postmortem published as at 22 Oct; no customer-count figure exists.

items.headline: Four men died building a chip factory
items.gist: Tue 20 Oct, four workers fell from height during steel-structure hoisting at TSMC's under-construction Fab 22, Southern Taiwan Science Park, Kaohsiung; the fourth died in hospital, toll confirmed 21 Oct. All four employed by subcontractor Shang Hao Machinery. The Southern Taiwan Science Park Bureau's preliminary assessment points to aged or broken bolts on a steel connection plate. The site had 3 labour inspections in 2025 and 18 in 2026, including a steel-structure inspection on 8 July; two other contractors previously fined a combined NT$210,000 (about US$6,467). TSMC voluntarily suspended steel-structure work at Kaohsiung and at all its new fab construction sites across Taiwan; work resumes only after Shang Hao's improvement plan passes review. Fab 22 is a leading-edge 2nm site for data-centre HPC chips. No schedule impact disclosed by anyone. Tom's Hardware counts at least nine construction deaths across TSMC sites since 2024. No TSMC spokesperson named in any report.

items.headline: SpaceX spent nearly four dollars for every one it earned
items.gist: Q3 2026 reported 20 Oct, figures from the company release: revenue $14,575m (from $5,576m, +161%); net income $4,404m against a $(1,054)m loss a year earlier - first quarterly profit as a public company; diluted EPS $0.35 v $(0.36). Segments: SI $7,560m revenue (from $813m) and $431m operating income; Connectivity $5,248m and $2,367m; Space $1,767m and $(7)m, 35 launches (12 customer, 23 internal) v 44. Starlink consumer subscribers 13.6m (from 7.2m), consumer ARPU $69/month down from $83. Capex $19,593m in the quarter, of which $16.4bn in SI; nine-month capex $48,069m against nine-month net cash from operating activities of $13,097m, i.e. $3.67 out per dollar in. On the call Musk said SpaceX and Tesla have each formed special committees of independent directors, at shareholders' request, to discuss a merger, and that he cannot participate as a conflicted party: 'Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes' and 'This is definitely kind of a question where I feel like I'm tap dancing through a minefield.' SpaceX about $2.1tn, Tesla about $1.5tn; Musk owns about 20% of Tesla and about 48% of SpaceX (about 82% of the vote); Barclays' Dan Levy expects an all-stock deal at roughly 0.7 SpaceX shares per Tesla share pre-premium; Tesla must hold its annual meeting by 6 Dec. Tesla Q3 same day: revenue $28.05bn flat, gross margin 19.6%, GAAP net income $787m -43%, non-GAAP EPS $0.48, deliveries 486,532 -2.1%, FY capex guidance cut to about $20bn from more than $25bn, shares -3.3% after hours. Outlets conflict on SpaceX's year-ago comparative loss (company release $1,054m; Fortune wrote $5.5bn) and on the combined valuation ($3.5tn to $3.7tn).

items.headline: Korean investors asked for 388 times the shares, then sold
items.gist: Elice priced its KOSDAQ IPO at 90,500 won, the top of a 70,400-90,500 range, raising 201.1bn won (about $150m); institutional demand 388.84x subscribed, retail 408.26x, with over 10 trillion won in deposits. It opened Tue 20 Oct at 75,700 won (-16.4%), traded as low as 61,000 (-32.6%) and last traded 65,300 (-27.8%). Headline falls differ by outlet because of intraday low v close: Reuters -28%, CNBC -30%, Bloomberg -32%, The Edge -33%. Follows Firmus pulling its Australian float on 9 Oct. US data-centre shares slid on the read-across; by Thu 22 Oct Asian chipmakers were sold hard - SK Hynix -4%, Samsung Electronics -3.6%, Kospi -2.1%, Hang Seng -2.7%, CSI 300 -1.6%; the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had just had its longest losing streak since October 2008. Against that, Lam Research's Q1 FY2027 (21 Oct): revenue $8.22bn +54% y/y, non-GAAP EPS $2.20, gross margin 52.4%, operating margin 40.2% - first above 40% - record FCF $3.24bn, and guidance that wafer fab equipment spending of the mid-$150bn range in CY2026 will preliminarily exceed $200bn in CY2027; shares still fell about 7% on supply-chain constraints that could delay shipments. At GTC Berlin on 21 Oct Jensen Huang said 'Demand is extraordinary. Capacity is the constraint', announced a $1.1bn capacity-reservation advance to King Yuan Electronics for new US test facilities, a multibillion-dollar advance to IBIDEN, substrate capacity up 2.5x over three years, and nearly $10bn committed across Europe with over 12,000 partners.

items.headline: Meta's bill for one week came to thirty-five billion dollars
items.gist: Judge Francis Mathew entered final judgment on Wed 21 Oct 2026 in New Mexico v Meta Platforms, ordering Meta to pay the state $25bn. A Santa Fe jury had found on 25 September that 26 of 29 statements by Meta and its leadership about data privacy were misleading, amounting to more than 43 million violations of New Mexico consumer protection law at up to $5,000 each; Mathew found a penalty above $219bn warranted under the statute and reduced it to $25bn. The state filed in 2021; the case stems from the personality quiz that harvested about 87 million Facebook profiles for Cambridge Analytica. AG Raul Torrez called it a warning 'to those in this space and beyond that we intend to protect our people' and one of the largest single-state verdicts in US history; Meta chief legal officer C.J. Mahoney said it 'makes it all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico'; Meta expects to prevail on appeal and D.A. Davidson's Gil Luria expects years of appeals. Separately, Meta's Q3 2026 results (21 Oct) carried a $9.89bn G&A charge for an August 2026 agreement with 52 state attorneys general over teen mental health providing payments of up to about $18.59bn: revenue $64.601bn +26% (consensus $63.31bn), costs $51.613bn +68%, operating income $12.988bn -37% with margin 20% v 40%, net income $9.860bn +264%, diluted EPS $3.83 against about $6.67 expected but $7.40 ex-charge. Q3 capex $34.91bn; FCF negative $2.12bn; headcount 66,775 -15%; DAP 3.64bn +3%. Guidance: Q4 revenue $73-76bn, FY26 expenses $175-179bn, FY26 capex $135-145bn with the floor raised from $130bn, Reality Labs loss $18-19bn narrowing to about $15bn in 2027. Board also approved a publicly listed non-voting Class C stock effective 19 Jan 2027, a one-for-one stock dividend after which Class A is expected to reflect a 2-for-1 split, with a Founder Alignment Agreement signed with Mark Zuckerberg.

items.headline: Washington ordered DeepSeek out, and anything built on it
items.gist: DHS Notice of Order, docket DHS-2026-0628, 91 FR 66346-66350, on public inspection 19 Oct and published 20 Oct, under the Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act 2018 (41 U.S.C. 1321-1328) following a Federal Acquisition Security Council recommendation. It bars federal civilian agencies from procuring IT products or services developed by Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co. and affiliates and requires removal of DeepSeek products plus 'third-party products and services developed using DeepSeek implementations'; exceptions may be requested. Signed for DHS by general counsel James H. Percival II. Builds on a December 2025 law restricting DeepSeek in intelligence national security systems. Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning opposed 'overstretching the concept of national security and politicizing technology and trade issues' and said Beijing would safeguard its firms' interests. Aggregator claims of a 60-day compliance window and an underlying order dated 24 July could not be confirmed and were not printed. Same day DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer under Apache 2.0, the inference framework behind its production services, supporting Nvidia SM100 GPUs and Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs, targeting DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash; it ships without a KV cache system, so it is offline inference rather than a complete service.

items.headline: Anthropic has drafted the law that could stop its own models
items.gist: Anthropic is circulating a draft federal AI safety bill, broken by Politico on 16 Oct and reported by TechCrunch on 20 Oct. Mechanism: independent evaluators register with the US Commerce Department and assess frontier models; labs may pay them but payment cannot be contingent on results; on finding an imminent catastrophic risk an evaluator has 72 hours to notify Commerce, which must then petition a judge in Washington DC to halt the release - no federal agency could halt distribution on its own. Threshold is a 'foreseeable, imminent risk' of more than 50 deaths or more than $1bn in property damage arising from the creation or release of a biological weapon, a model evading its developer's controls, or a cyberattack - the same numbers as California SB 53. An Anthropic spokesperson said 'This bill represents the proposals outlined in Anthropic's Advanced AI Framework' and that Anthropic has pushed these since June. Daily Caller coverage names it the AEGIS Act and names Anthony Cimino of Anthropic policy, but the bill name is single-sourced and was not printed; TechCrunch says no name was given and Anthropic did not respond to it. No member of Congress has introduced it.

items.headline: A tank of petrol is now setting Britain's interest rate
items.gist: ONS consumer price inflation for September 2026, published 21 Oct: CPI 3.5% y/y, up from 3.1% in August and above expectations, the highest since October 2025; +0.4% m/m. Core 2.8% (from 2.6%), services 3.7% (from 3.4%), goods 3.2% (from 2.7%), CPIH 3.6% (from 3.3%). Largest upward contribution transport, mainly motor fuels: fuel prices +29.8% y/y (from 23.0%), petrol averaging 169.5p a litre (+8.2p in the month), diesel 192.5p (+10.7p); transport added 0.94 percentage points to the headline rate. Largest drag restaurants and hotels, with hotel prices +2.3% y/y. Bank Rate 3.75%, unchanged since 2023; MPC meets 5 November; next CPI 18 November. Danni Hewson of AJ Bell: 'Market expectation of a November increase is now nearing 100%', with a better-than-even chance of a second hike before year end. UK unemployment fell to 4.7%. Set against a Reuters poll of 100 economists taken 16-20 Oct: 94 expect the Fed to hold on 27-28 Oct and all 100 expect a December hike, up from fewer than half last month; nearly 60% see the peak at 4.00-4.25%. The Bank of Korea held at 3.00% unanimously on 22 Oct after hikes in July and August; Hungary's MNB held at 5.50% on 20 Oct; China held its loan prime rates at 3.00% and 3.50% on 20 Oct for a 17th month.

items.headline: Jakarta defended the rupiah without touching its main rate
items.gist: Bank Indonesia's Board of Governors met 20-21 October and held the BI-Rate at 5.75%, the level reached after four hikes totalling 100bp in 2026. The actual action was asymmetric: the Deposit Facility rate was raised 25bp to 5.00% while the Lending Facility was held at 6.50% - a rupiah defence rather than a growth move. Reserve requirements cut for conventional banks from 9% to 8% on 1 Nov and to 7% on 1 Dec (sharia 7.5% to 6.5% to 5.5%); the macroprudential liquidity incentive cut from 6% to 5% from 1 Dec; DNDF hedging premium discounts for foreign-funded transactions raised from 25% to 40% at six months and 30% to 45% at twelve. BI says the incentive regime has drawn US$9.9bn of foreign inflows since June 2026. Jakarta Composite closes: 5,863.78 on 15 Oct, 5,185.11 on 16 Oct (-11.57%), 4,996.60 on 19 Oct (-3.64%, lowest since 2020), 5,278.89 on 20 Oct (+5.65%), +1.27% on 21 Oct, +1.1% intraday on 22 Oct against a falling Asia. Rupiah Rp17,985 on 20 Oct per BI, then closed Rp18,022 on 21 Oct (-0.17%), back through 18,000 on the day BI held. Record foreign outflows of Rp88.19tn in 2026, against Rp53.84tn in all of 2020 and Rp50.17tn in all of 2008; index down about 40% year to date. September CPI 3.28% y/y, core 2.84%, target 2.5% +/-1%; credit +13.26% y/y; 2026 growth forecast 4.9-5.7%. OJK's Hasan Fawzi cited 'measured enforcement' and Rp2.1tn of fines; reform package includes disclosure of holders above 1% and a roadmap to a 15% minimum free float. MSCI's decision is due on or before 30 June 2027, comments close 30 April 2027. Note: Antara's own report is internally inconsistent on whether Destry Damayanti is Governor or Deputy Governor, so no name was printed; the Governor is Perry Warjiyo.

items.headline: Ambani's $3.2bn was covered in under two hours
items.gist: Jio Platforms opened India's largest-ever share sale on 21 Oct and was fully covered in under two hours, the institutional tranche in about ten minutes. Size Rs30,213 crore, about US$3.2bn, entirely a fresh issue of 270,000,000 shares with no offer for sale; price band Rs1,065-1,119, face value Rs10, lot 12 shares, minimum retail Rs13,428. Bidding 21-23 Oct, anchor book 19 Oct, allotment about 26 Oct, listing tentatively 28 Oct on BSE and NSE. Valuation up to US$108.3bn (Rs10,30,490 crore post-issue market cap, post-issue P/E 33.19x, EPS Rs33.72), against Bharti Airtel at US$123.38bn the same day. Anchor allotment US$853m (Rs8,109.85 crore) including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock, with anchor bids above US$25bn. Day 1 close 3.16x; day 2 (22 Oct) 3.47x overall with QIB 9.42x. Allocation QIB 50%, NII 15%, retail 35%; about Rs27,500 crore of proceeds to prepay borrowings at subsidiary RJIL. BRLM Kotak Mahindra Capital, registrar KFin Technologies. FY2026 PAT Rs30,052.70 crore, up about 15%, revenue up about 16%; Reuters puts it at about $3.2bn profit on $15.5bn revenue in the year to March. First Reliance group IPO since 2006. For pace: NSE's sale was 42% subscribed on day one and Hyundai Motor India 18%.

editions.title: Signal — 26 October
editions.lede: Two long-serving leaders lost their jobs this weekend. Five American banks changed the locks.

items.headline: Brazil's voters changed their minds in three weeks
items.gist: Lula won the 25 Oct runoff with 51.78% against Flavio Bolsonaro's 48.22%, 100% counted, a margin of about 4.4m votes, after losing the first round 45-47. Bolsonaro refuses to concede and wants the result annulled, citing Justice Cristiano Zanin's two-hour extension of polling granted three minutes before close (both campaigns had asked for it). Lula is 81; fourth term begins 5 Jan 2027. A Tokyo-listed Brazil ETF fell almost 15% on Monday's Asian open; Goldman's bad case was BRL -10%, long yields +200bp, equities -15%. Chicago soybeans hit a two-month low.

items.headline: Serbia's students won, and Vucic read out the numbers himself
items.gist: Vucic conceded on 25 Oct after 14 years in power (SNS governing since 2012), reading a sample count giving the Student List 135-140 of 250 seats against 105 for his own; 126 is a majority. 'It is clear that we have lost these elections.' Turnout 64.9% by 6pm, highest since 1992. Movement grew from the Nov 2024 Novi Sad canopy collapse that killed 16. CRTA logged pressure at almost a third of 500 monitored stations; CeSID about 260 irregularity reports. Von der Leyen congratulated the students.

items.headline: Five American banks changed the locks on AI
items.gist: Axios reported 22 Oct that Morgan Stanley has begun blocking third-party AI agents and that JPMorgan, Bank of America, Citi and Wells Fargo are restricting them; confirmations followed 23 Oct. Core conflict: an agent needs the customer's username and password, which bank terms forbid sharing. Executives tracked agents telephoning call centres and acting unasked, and say they cannot reliably tell agent from human or authorised from rogue. Jamie Dimon told analysts on 13 Oct rogue agents may number in the thousands. Emerging compromise is read-only access via intermediaries such as Plaid. Schwab reportedly exploring Model Context Protocol links.

items.headline: Google's Finnish diggers are parked until the paperwork catches up
items.gist: Finland's Licensing and Supervision Authority ordered Tuike Finland (Google) to suspend environmentally significant preparatory work at BOTH Muhos and Kajaani until environmental impact assessments are complete; reported 23 Oct. Order names trees felled, topsoil stripped, roads and storage yards built, ditches and culverts moved. Guardian estimates 250,000 trees cleared at Muhos. Tommi Muilu, head of the environment department: 'The measures in question will change the environment and cause impacts.' Planning, measurement and soil surveys may continue. Sites belong to a EUR13bn September investment. Over 96,000 Finns have signed a citizens' initiative for tighter data-centre rules including a fee. Google did not comment. Thread closed: the question we asked is answered.

items.headline: Britain is asking Brussels to let its cloud companies bid
items.gist: Bloomberg, 23 Oct: the UK is seeking a carve-out from the EU's draft Cloud and AI Development Act, which sorts public-sector procurement into four sovereignty assurance levels, the strictest closed to foreign-owned or foreign-controlled suppliers. London objects to the EU operational-presence requirement and the ownership-control limits; BT and Nscale would be affected. UK says it breaches the UK-EU trade agreement; the Commission disagrees. France and Germany have floated letting UK firms access certain EU industrial subsidies if Britain aligns on foreign investment screening and subsidised Chinese imports. Jonathan Reynolds: UK might tariff Chinese EVs but on British terms. London-Brussels summit 20 Nov. Separately, on 23 Oct the Council adopted its position on 'EU Inc', a 28th optional corporate regime with two-day online registration at up to EUR100, 21 months to implement.

items.headline: Seoul's chip boom has lost two fifths of its value
items.gist: Kospi closed 5,550.30 on Fri 23 Oct, fell to about 5,455 intraday Monday; more than 40% below its June high, about -19% in October, still roughly +27% year to date. Goldman cut its 12-month target from 12,000 to 9,000 on 26 Oct, a 25% cut that still implies about 62% upside; it blames valuation rather than earnings, notes Korea trades near 4x forward earnings (cheapest major market) and that current memory prices imply a 65% fall in 2027 earnings, which it calls too pessimistic. Ex-memory, about half the index trades at 7.6x. Memory and storage shares have lost $1.3tn from 2026 highs: about $489bn at SK Hynix, $411bn at Micron; 58 of 59 chip stocks in Yahoo Finance's basket fell in October.

items.headline: SK Hynix shelved a float worth up to $150bn
items.gist: SK Hynix shelved the US listing of Solidigm, its flash-memory unit bought from Intel, on 23 Oct, citing market conditions and share price. WSJ put the planned raise at $10-15bn at a valuation up to $150bn. SK Hynix's own July US listing priced at $149 and raised a record $26.5bn (largest-ever US listing by a foreign company); the stock traded $136.83 on 23 Oct, about a third below September's record. SK Hynix shares rose about 4% on the news. It still wants a US fab for high-capacity SSDs and is still seeking funding. Joins Firmus (cancelled) and AirTrunk (delayed to 2027).

items.headline: The vaccine worked, and Moderna lost a quarter of its value
items.gist: Phase 3 INTerpath-001: intismeran autogene (individualised mRNA, up to 34 neoantigens) plus Keytruda cut risk of recurrence or death by 42% versus Keytruda alone after a median 24.6 months; distant metastasis-free risk -38%. Full data at ESMO Saturday 24 Oct after a social-media leak forced early release on 22 Oct. Moderna shares fell nearly 25%, Merck about 1%. Analysts had wanted 40-50%; Moderna had said 35% would be clinically meaningful; Phase 2 showed 44%. 7% of vaccine patients discontinued for an adverse event versus 5%. RBC's Trung Huynh: 'While approval seems likely, commercial success is far less certain.' Kidney interim data late 2026 or H1 2027. BioNTech's rival vaccine recently failed in colorectal cancer.

items.headline: Oil reached $117 while the president wondered aloud
items.gist: Brent closed Fri 23 Oct at $116.72, +3.1% on the day and +6.2% on the week, from under $97 at the start of October; WTI $103.27, +3.8%. Dow -652.82 (-1.2%), worst day in two months; S&P 500 -0.52% to 7,623.68; Nasdaq -0.21% to 25,955.34; selling spread into staples, utilities and health care. IRGC claimed on 22 Oct it struck four ships on the southern route near Oman with three more hitting mines, uncorroborated. UAE closed Umm Al Quwain beaches after a spill traced to the Gem No. 2, hit 9 Oct. Iranian state TV said non-compliant vessels have stopped transiting. Trump, 25 Oct: claimed the US now controls the Strait of Hormuz and asked 'do I make a deal with them, or do I finish them off?'; said no strike that day; on 23 Oct accused Iran of inventing attacks to raise oil prices before the 3 Nov midterms, and is reported to have told officials strikes wait until after. Brent eased to $115.48 Monday.

items.headline: Korea has one gigawatt of data centres. SK wants fifteen.
items.gist: SK Hyper, SK Telecom's data-centre arm, is seeking about $350bn (463 trillion won) for its first 5GW, reported 23 Oct by Bloomberg and the Seoul Economic Daily; full plan is 15GW in Korea by 2035, first capacity operating 2029. CEO Chung Suk-keun says Korea's entire data-centre market is about 1GW today, so phase one is five times the existing industry. Over 2GW planned in Yeongnam starting with Ulsan, plus gigawatt-scale sites in Chungcheong and the south-west. Talking to hyperscalers about siting inference work in Korea; first outside investment targeted late 2026 or early 2027. SK Telecom has committed up to 750bn won by 2030, about 0.16% of phase one. Chung names demand and capital, not power or land, as the binding constraints.

items.headline: DeepSeek raised $15bn and wants to list before OpenAI
items.gist: WSJ, 22 Oct: DeepSeek raised $15bn in its second private round, nearly double target, at about $74bn pre-close. Investors include Tencent, CATL, Geely, Legend Capital, Stony Creek Capital, plus existing backers Monolith Management and Shixiang. Citic Securities hired for a Shanghai listing in early 2027, potentially beating OpenAI to public markets; Yan Wentao joined as CFO in September. Still trains hardest models on Nvidia; working with Huawei to shift training to Chinese chips. Liang Wenfeng told investors in September annualised revenue reached $1bn, up from $400-500m in July, almost all developer API; claims 70-80% gross margin on V4 while undercutting US rivals.

items.headline: Japan is going to Phobos for ten grams
items.gist: JAXA's Martian Moons eXploration launched on an H3 (its 10th flight) from Tanegashima pad 2 at 1941 GMT on 19 Oct, 4:41am 20 Oct Japan time. Mars arrival August 2027, about three years in the system, two touchdowns on Phobos, roughly 10g of sample. French-German IDEFIX rover deploys late 2028 or early 2029. Departs Mars November 2030; capsule lands in Australia 2031. First-ever Phobos landing and sample return; Russia's Phobos-Grunt failed in 2011-12. NASA has invested about $87m, supplied the MEGANE spectrometer and a Honeybee pneumatic sampler plus Deep Space Network support, and gets at least 15% of the sample. Open question the samples settle: captured asteroid or giant-impact debris.

editions.title: Signal — 29 October
editions.lede: Canada raised interest rates on Wednesday for the first time in more than three years. The reason sits in a strait that has now been shut for 241 days.
sections: Nothing to do with the money

items.headline: Four tankers a day, where there used to be eighty-five
items.gist: Day 241 of closure. Iran said 28 Oct the strait could reopen in 4-5 days if the US lifts its naval blockade of Iranian ports; Tehran talks on 26 Oct ended with no ceasefire and no joint statement. IMF PortWatch counted 4 tanker transits on 18 Oct against an 85 pre-war baseline. War-risk insurance 6-10% of hull value per transit, against 0.15-0.25% before the war. IMO said 27 Oct the route holds mines and it cannot guarantee safe transit. Brent settled $115.32 on 28 Oct, +1.3%, about 60% above pre-war. Betting markets price normal traffic by 31 Dec at about 12%. Washington has said no strike before the 3 Nov midterms.

items.headline: Canada raised rates to stop petrol becoming everything else
items.gist: Bank of Canada raised the overnight rate 25bp to 2.50% on 28 Oct, first increase since July 2023; Bank Rate 2.75%, deposit 2.45%. CPI near 3% since April, expected about 3.5% by year-end, driven by persistently high oil. Excluding gasoline, September inflation was 2.2% and core near 2%. Council considered holding, then judged pass-through risk had risen. Statement: 'there could be a need to increase the policy rate further'; Macklem: decisions 'one meeting at a time'. Inflation forecast to average 3% in 2027, back to 2% around mid-2028. Q2 growth 3.3%, Q3 about 2%.

items.headline: Two votes at the Fed were for a rise, and they lost
items.gist: FOMC held the target range at 3.75-4.00% on 28 Oct, vote 10-2. Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack both dissented in favour of a 25bp RISE - two hawkish dissents in one meeting. Statement: activity expanding at a strong pace, job gains keeping pace with the workforce, 'inflation remains elevated', 'The Committee will deliver price stability.' Chair Kevin Warsh said the 'monetary medicine' was 'starting to work some, but there's no firm conclusions', and that he 'didn't hear an utterance about politics'. Futures price about 85% odds of a 25bp rise on 9 December, up from about 80% a week earlier. 10-year closed near 5.04%; H.15 for 26 Oct put the 10-year at 5.00%, 30-year 5.31%, effective funds rate 3.88%. S&P 500 closed +0.28% at 7,743.98, a third straight gain.

items.headline: Britain taxed its banks to pay for the heating
items.gist: John Healey's first Budget, 28 Oct. Bank surcharge doubled from 3% to 6% for 15 months from January, raising about GBP1.2bn. GBP100 Household Energy Payment to about 20m households in council tax bands A-D, costing GBP2.6bn; electricity VAT cut extended to July (about GBP50 off the cap); gas standing charges scrapped next year for about 23m homes, average saving about GBP45; 5p fuel duty cut extended to July 2027. Small business rates relief threshold up from GBP12,000 to GBP18,000. GBP10bn more support for Ukraine. Measures add GBP12.4bn to borrowing over three years. OBR: CPI 3.5% next year against 2% previously; growth 1.25% this year to 1% next; debt interest GBP109bn this year (3.5% of GDP) against GBP39bn in 2019-20, rising to GBP160bn by 2031-32, with about GBP14bn of this year's rise attributed to the Middle East; GBP15bn headroom in 2029-30, GBP24bn against the PSNFL target. Gilt yields eased; NatWest and Lloyds +1.5%, Barclays +1.1%.

items.headline: France borrows at 4.94 per cent. Germany pays 3.37.
items.gist: French 10-year OAT 4.94% on 28 Oct against a 3.37% Bund; spread 156.6bp, down from a 174.6bp peak on 22 Oct, against a one-year average of 79.8bp and a 2011 record of 225.1bp. Cause is domestic: no budget majority, debt path, and suggestions from parts of the left that ECB-held French debt could be written off. ECB met 29 Oct, expected to hold the deposit rate at 2.5% after two rises since June; money markets price about three more, to 3.25%. Intervention unlikely for now; the Transmission Protection Instrument remains unused. Reuters reported the World Economic Forum could name Lagarde its next chair as early as November, a year before her term ends; Klaas Knot and Pablo Hernandez de Cos named as frontrunners.

items.headline: Google made twenty-six billion dollars and still ran short
items.gist: Alphabet Q3 2026 (reported 28 Oct): revenue $127,577m, +25%; Google Cloud $30,709m, +103% from $15,157m; operating income $40,576m (32% margin); net income $26,468m; diluted EPS $2.12 against $2.87, cut 55c by an $8.7bn equity-securities loss; capex $51,355m against about $24bn a year earlier; operating cash flow $42,290m; FREE CASH FLOW NEGATIVE $9,065m, worse than -$5.9bn in Q2; TTM FCF $19,747m. Shares fell as much as 10% after hours. Microsoft FY27 Q1 same evening: revenue $92,279m +19%, operating income $45,915m, net income $36,629m +32%, diluted EPS $4.92, Microsoft Cloud $63.9bn +30%, Azure +48% (revenue $33,165m), commercial RPO $677bn +73%, additions to property and equipment $39,367m against $19,394m; stayed cash-positive; shares +2.6% after hours.

items.headline: Oracle promised to stop borrowing, and the shares jumped
items.gist: Oracle Investor Day, 28 Oct: new capital-market funding for the FY27-FY30 cycle capped at $20bn, split $10bn equity and $10bn gross debt, excluding refinancing and on top of a $20bn ATM equity raise completed in Q1 FY27. Targets: FY30 revenue $225bn+ (over 35% CAGR from FY26), non-GAAP operating margin 40%+, non-GAAP EPS $21+; FY27 guidance reaffirmed at $90bn+ revenue and $8.10 EPS. Free cash flow positive in H2 FY28, at least $30bn in FY29, self-funded growth from FY29, net debt below 3.5x adjusted EBITDA in FY29; capex peaks FY27-FY28 then steps down; vendor financing, customer hardware and prepayments to reduce upfront cash. Shares +11%. Vertiv +17% the same day on AI-infrastructure forecasts. Context: Oracle five-year CDS hit a record 288bp on 15 Oct.

items.headline: America's largest gas producer was assembled for the data centres
items.gist: EQT agreed 26 Oct to buy Range Resources all-stock, 0.987 EQT shares per Range share, valuing Range equity at about $12.83bn ($54.91/share), a premium of nearly 21%; Range holders take 27%; closing expected Q1 2027; two Range directors join the board. Combined: over 9 Bcf/d including NGLs (largest US producer), 2.8m net acres, 30+ years of inventory, 3,700 miles of pipeline, about $50bn enterprise value; $300m long-term and $325m near-term synergies. CEO Toby Rice called it 'America's natural gas champion' and said it could scale to 17 and eventually 20 Bcf/d. Demand case: gas-fired power for AI data centres plus Gulf Coast LNG exports into a Europe and Asia short of gas because of the Iran war. Infralogic's Patrick Harris flagged three risks: a Russia-Ukraine peace deal, normalised Middle East LNG flows, slower AI adoption. Range +11%, EQT -8%.

items.headline: The memory makers are keeping four fifths of what they charge
items.gist: SK hynix Q3 2026 (27 Oct): revenue KRW104,615.5bn, first quarter above 100tn, +32% q/q and +328% y/y; operating profit KRW83,333.8bn, +632% y/y; operating margin 80% against 47% a year earlier; net profit KRW39,775.6bn. FY2026 shareholder returns about KRW100tn: at least 30tn dividends, at least 60tn buybacks/cancellations; Q3 dividend KRW20,000/share (half a special dividend from Kioxia gains); a further KRW20tn repurchase approved; cash KRW114.5tn, net cash KRW98.7tn. CEO Kwak Noh-Jung confirmed the Solidigm IPO review is discontinued, closing the listing shelved on 26 Oct at up to $150bn. Samsung Q3 (29 Oct): revenue KRW195,253bn +126.9%, operating profit KRW107,440bn +783.1%, margin 55.0% against 14.1%; nine-month operating profit KRW254.17tn; DRAM ASPs +about 20% q/q, NAND up high teens, bit shipments up only single digits; HBM4 sales up; dividend KRW4,601/share, about KRW30tn, matching expectations, with the rest of the 90-110tn 2026 return plan left to a late-January board meeting. Market: Kospi hit a record 6,100.11 intraday on 29 Oct then fell to about 5,920, -1.5%; Samsung -5.0% to KRW230,000 after +9.01% the day before; SK hynix +2.5% to KRW1,524,000; won 1,332/USD. Korea's finance ministry and the Bank of Korea said they were watching volatility.

items.headline: China is making the chip anyway, and discarding most of it
items.gist: Reuters reported 28 Oct, citing people familiar, that only about 20-30% of ChangXin Memory's (CXMT) high-bandwidth memory chips meet specification. CXMT, China's largest DRAM maker, plans limited HBM3E production within two months and has sent samples to several Chinese AI chip designers. Its parts reportedly perform closer to SK hynix's older HBM3 than to HBM3E; SK hynix's comparable yield is around 70%. Drivers: US export controls on memory and equipment, and Beijing's push for domestic alternatives to Nvidia. Context: Stargate-scale projects need hundreds of thousands more DRAM wafers a month, about 40% of global output (Tom's Hardware); SK hynix, Samsung, Kioxia and CXMT are together worth over $2tn and supply about a third of big tech's data-centre spend (Bloomberg).

items.headline: A Japanese internet company told its customers to unplug
items.gist: GMO Internet told customers to disconnect PCs from the network, shut them down and unplug cables. Timeline: malicious programs confirmed in some customer server environments 20 Oct; all Onamae Desktop Cloud plans shut from 4am 21 Oct, 26,739 servers identified as potentially affected; ransom email the same day demanding about JPY8bn (roughly $50m); police consulted 22 Oct and GMO refused to pay, saying payment would guarantee neither deletion nor non-use; compensation and alternative service offered 24 Oct; customer devices collected 25-26 Oct. Attackers threatened to publish data and launch ransomware at noon JST 27 Oct; alleged company and customer data appeared at 12:30pm; at 1:55pm GMO said no ransomware attack was confirmed and the material was still being verified. Onamae Desktop Cloud rents virtual desktops to financial traders; customers told to reset passwords after reports of unauthorised operations on trading accounts. Japan's FSA called for better 'vulnerability management, defense-in-depth and incident preparedness'. Attacker group not named; GMO's own unit separately reported the Artex AI pentesting tool used against Japanese firms, not publicly linked to this breach.

items.headline: DeepMind's new model builds a world that answers back
items.gist: Google DeepMind released Genie 4 on 27 Oct as a research preview to trusted testers. Real-time interactive world simulation steered in natural language: move the camera, change the weather, add characters and objects; characters hold real-time dialogue; each world generates its own ambient sound and music. Scenes stay consistent up to two minutes, double Genie 3's limit (Genie 3 shipped a little over a year earlier). Gemini plans steps and checks frames while Genie generates visuals; Gemini Omni grounds appearance and behaviour. Rolling out to Google AI Ultra subscribers via Project Genie and to Gemini API and AI Studio early-access partners in coming weeks. Acknowledged limits: object drift over longer runs, no solution for audio accuracy or legible in-world text, product experience unclear. Quotes: Tejas Kulkarni on 'hybrid world models, where you have a combination of Gemini writing code and text'; engineer Diego Rivas on flow in creative ideation. DeepMind frames world simulation as a step toward AGI, naming safe training environments for robots and agents.
