editions.title: Signal — 2 November
editions.lede: Six point three billion dollars left Binance on Thursday afternoon. The exchange locked the door four hours later.

items.headline: The biggest theft on record took twenty minutes
items.gist: About $6.3bn (TRM: $6.36bn moved, $6.23bn at prices) left Binance hot wallets across ten blockchains from 20:05 GMT on 29 Oct, most of it in ~20 minutes; ~$3.8bn ether, ~$1.5bn bitcoin (18,270 BTC), one transfer over $2.5bn. TRM Labs attributes with high confidence to TraderTraitor (North Korea, Lazarus); FBI named the same group for the $1.5bn Bybit theft in Feb 2025, so this is ~4x larger; Elliptic's chief scientist called it almost certainly the largest known theft of any kind. Method: on Ethereum an EIP-7702 delegation turned a Binance hot wallet into an attacker-controlled sweeper, with 50 pre-signed authorisations, one matching the nonce; the other nine chains used ordinary signed transfers, suggesting compromised signing infrastructure. Preparation began at least 36 hours earlier with small Tornado Cash withdrawals. Binance first blamed an engineer's compromised laptop and has published no root cause. Freezes: Tether began 21:01 GMT, blocked Binance's hot wallet 22:06, Circle followed 22:09 and blocked at 23:53; ~$2.7bn frozen per TRM as at 00:30 GMT 30 Oct ($1.77bn USDT, $825m USDC, $40.5m RLUSD, $27.8m USD1, 8,426 ETH plus $74.6m ARB), later reported near $3bn; ~$1.5bn could not be frozen; ~$2.4bn still with the attacker including over 420,000 ETH and 18,270 BTC. Binance revoked the attacker's hot-wallet permissions only at 00:10 GMT, four hours five minutes after the first transfer. Binance set aside $6bn, said it will absorb the loss not pass it to users, replenished 90% by 31 Oct, resumed withdrawals 1 Nov, promised proof of reserves 2 Nov. Bitcoin fell about 5% below $80,000; Coinbase and Robinhood fell. Attacker sold ~325m USDT to market makers at a discount above 10% for ~122,300 ETH. US Secret Service tracking; FBI published wallet addresses.

items.headline: Intel's worst day in fifty-two years
items.gist: Intel shares fell about 29% on Fri 30 Oct, worst day since 1974 (some outlets -27.3% to -28.6% depending on measure). Q3 2026 beat: revenue $16.5bn, non-GAAP EPS $0.52, gross margin 44.1%; Data Center and AI $7.3bn with $3bn operating profit, fastest sector growth in 15 years. Q4 guidance: revenue $15-16bn, non-GAAP EPS $0.25, gross margin 38%. Causes: client computing to fall more than 20% q/q on the PC correction driven by memory prices; and an early-October explosion at Fab 28, Kiryat Gat, Israel, which shut the plant about two weeks. CFO David Zinsner: about $300m of Q4 revenue and ~200bp of gross margin, with a similar hit in Q1 (roughly $600m across both); nearly all of it 10nm server products; Intel 3 yields a separate headwind named by CEO Lip-Bu Tan. Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon said margin would have been 40% without Israel; Zinsner did not dispute it. Two workers died and one was injured; neither release nor call mentioned them. Zinsner: 'demand for DCAI products continues to meaningfully exceed available supply', constrained through 2027 into 2028; addressable server CPU market possibly $40bn to over $200bn in five years. Knock-on: AMD -12%, Nvidia -5%, VanEck Semiconductor ETF -8%; nearly 70% of US issues fell; Vix +32% intraday, highest since June.

items.headline: Reddit's visitors stopped arriving
items.gist: Reddit Q3 2026 reported 29 Oct: revenue $895m, +53% y/y; diluted EPS $1.40. US average daily active uniques 50.7m, -5% q/q and -2% y/y, the first annual fall since the 2024 IPO; global DAU about 130.3m, roughly flat q/q. Search referrals fell through the quarter and by more than 1 million a week on average in October, accelerating late in Q3; logged-out web traffic hit hardest. CEO Steve Huffman named Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode as the 'leading hypothesis' but said Reddit cannot see Google's ranking changes; he also suggested machine-translated Reddit content may rank lower outside the US. Q4 guidance $1.00-1.03bn revenue, with a warning that total daily uniques could fall a low double-digit percentage from a 130m base if referrals keep declining. Reddit will test a mostly logged-in experience in selected non-US markets in Q4, which also reduces AI scraping; over 80% of monetisation already comes from logged-in and app users. Shares -29.22% on 30 Oct to $91.73.

items.headline: Amazon spent $42bn more cash than it took in
items.gist: Follow-up to 29 Oct. Amazon Q3 2026 (reported 29 Oct): net sales $201.9bn +12%; operating income $28.1bn (13.9% margin); net income $20.7bn, diluted EPS $1.89 against $1.95, the fall explained by $9.5bn of prior-year pre-tax Anthropic gains; AWS $46.0bn +39%, $184bn annualised run rate. Trailing-twelve-month operating cash flow $168.3bn +29%; TTM free cash flow MINUS $42.4bn; nine-month purchases of property and equipment $175.7bn ($172.2bn net of proceeds and incentives); implied TTM capex net of proceeds about $210.7bn. 2026 cash capex guidance about $220bn, unchanged. Q4 guidance: net sales $240-247bn (+12-16%), operating income $28.5-33.5bn. Alphabet had reported FCF of minus $9.1bn on 28 Oct. Over the week Alphabet fell 12.6% and SpaceX 8.7%. Thread closed: Amazon's answer is in.

items.headline: Ottawa bought a piece of its biggest AI company
items.gist: Announced 29 Oct on day one of the Canada-EU summit in Montreal: Canada will invest up to C$1.6bn for an equity stake in Cohere via the Canada Development Investment Corporation. Round about C$7bn (reported as ~US$5bn), valuing Cohere near C$35.7-36bn, Canada's most valuable private tech company. Germany's Schwarz Group (owner of Lidl) leads; Nvidia and Bell Canada also committed, amounts undisclosed. Conditions: Cohere keeps its Canadian headquarters and incorporation, creates 1,000 high-paying jobs, spends at least C$1.7bn on Canadian computing infrastructure by 2030, and reports progress to Ottawa; Carney said government data stays in Canada. Carney: 'And now, Canada has a stake in it'; 'Canadians decide how it works and who it answers to.' CEO Aidan Gomez said the company will always be based in Canada. Ottawa had pledged up to C$240m to a Cohere data-centre project in 2024. No percentage of the company disclosed. Separately, Telegraph reported 1 Nov that the UK Sovereign AI Fund is investing hundreds of millions of pounds in London inference-chip startup Fractile at a $6.5bn valuation; round size conflicts between accounts ($700m per Telegraph, $600m in earlier reports), with Anthropic reported to have agreed to buy about $250m of Fractile's chips. Not announced as at 2 Nov.

items.headline: Seoul will tax the chip boom to pay for the next one
items.gist: President Lee Jae Myung's fourth budget address, National Assembly, Mon 2 Nov: a record 2027 budget of 820.9 trillion won, 12.8% larger than 2026. 21.3tn won (about US$16bn) for AI and three 'megaprojects' - semiconductors, physical AI, AI data centres - nearly double this year's 10.8tn won. A 162tn won (about US$120.5bn) future-oriented fund backed by windfall tax revenue from the semiconductor boom; Lee called it 'a mechanism to keep public finances stable as tax revenue fluctuates more widely' and 'a platform for strategic investment to boost the economy's growth potential'. 13.8tn won for ten next-generation strategic technology fields. Welfare: automatic enrolment for major benefits, income benchmark for about 60 programmes up 6.7%, maximum monthly livelihood benefit for a four-person household 2.21m won. Ruling Democratic Party calls it 'a budget to prepare Korea's future'; opposition People Power Party called it 'a declaration of war on the people' and protested in the Assembly lobby, citing national debt. Legal passage deadline 2 December. CNBC reported Korea also targets a sovereign AI model of 'world's highest performance'; that element not confirmed in the Korea Times account.

items.headline: The Quad went looking for chokepoints
items.gist: Quad foreign ministers met 31 Oct in Atlanta alongside the G20 foreign ministers' meeting: India's S Jaishankar, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Japan's Toshimitsu Motegi, Australia's Penny Wong. Joint Press Release on Economic Prosperity and Security pledges more than $85m of technical and financial assistance to expand access to trusted AI across the Indo-Pacific, partly through the Quad AI Accelerator; no per-country split, allocation or timeline. The four will launch an effort to identify semiconductor and AI hardware supply-chain chokepoints 'before they cause disruptions'; no lead agency, method or timeline. 'Grave concerns' recorded about economic coercion including arbitrary export restrictions and non-market overcapacity, naming no country. Also: trusted 5G/6G/Open RAN cooperation, digital identity standards, condemnation of scam compounds, US $10m for critical-mineral recovery from e-waste in India and ASEAN, first Quad Business Leaders' Forum, and a Quad export credit agencies meeting in Tokyo on 18 November. Rubio: the four are 'delivering results for our people and the nations in the region.'

items.headline: Korea sold $115bn of things in a single month
items.gist: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources via Yonhap, 1 Nov: October 2026 exports a record $115.3bn, up 93.7% y/y, unadjusted (implying about $59bn a year earlier). Semiconductors $56.4bn, +259%, about 49% of total exports. Imports $72.78bn +36%; trade surplus $42.5bn. Other categories: petroleum products $6.92bn +80%, automobiles $6.55bn +18.1% on hybrid demand, petrochemicals $4bn +27.5%, cosmetics $1.44bn +57.5%. Destinations: China $26.98bn +133.6% (above $20bn for five straight months), US $24.9bn +185.8%, south-east Asia $21.33bn +128%, EU $8.1bn +56.4%. January-October cumulative exports passed $900bn for the first time; the ministry says annual exports could reach $1 trillion as early as November. Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan: 'The global trade environment remains uncertain', citing protectionism, supply chain shifts and Middle East tensions.

items.headline: China's factories went back below fifty
items.gist: National Bureau of Statistics, published 31 Oct: October official manufacturing PMI 49.3, down from 50.1 in September and below the 50.0 consensus; non-manufacturing PMI (services and construction) 49.7, also below the expansion line, which is unusual for that series. NBS directed attention to sub-indices it groups as 'new momentum' industries, which it says maintained rapid growth. Set against Korea's record October exports the same week: the chip-driven build-out is lifting component makers rather than the wider regional economy.

items.headline: France has not grown all year, and Lagarde is leaving
items.gist: Insee, Fri 30 Oct: French Q3 GDP -0.1% q/q, after 0.0% in Q2 and -0.2% in Q1, so no growth in 2026. Household consumption +0.4%; transport equipment output -3.5% (aerospace -4.5%, automotive -1.5%), agri-food -1.5% on poor summer harvests. French inflation 3.4% y/y in October, from 3.1%, highest since January 2024; Italy's October headline reported at 5.4%. Eurostat flash the same day: euro area Q3 GDP +0.4% q/q, EU +0.5%. Economy minister Roland Lescure said the economy is 'at a standstill' and France 'will hit the wall' without a 2027 budget; the government has no majority, with article 49.3 or ordinances (never used for a budget since 1958) as fallbacks. French 10-year OAT about 4.9% on 30 Oct, spread to Bunds about 155bp, down from the 174.6bp peak of 22 Oct against a one-year average near 80bp. BCA Research's Jeremie Peloso says a technical recession over coming quarters is 'highly likely'. ECB held the deposit rate at 2.5% on 29 Oct, citing rising energy prices as an upside inflation risk, with markets pricing a December rise and up to three more by end-2027 to 3.25%; euro-area private-sector growth in October was the weakest in four months. Christine Lagarde announced on 29 Oct that she leaves on 7 February 2027, nine months early. Quotes: 'We have an obligation of neutrality'; 'I don't think that I can be comfortable in that neutrality'; she wants 'the freedom to engage on matters that are not monetary policy matters'; in a video, 'I leave this institution with a sense of good work done and an ECB that is fit for the future.' A source said she wants to weigh in on French and global politics; WEF chairmanship remains speculation. Antonio Costa said the successor search starts immediately; Klaas Knot and Pablo Hernandez de Cos are the front-runners. Isabel Schnabel leaves the Executive Board in January for the IMF; chief economist Philip Lane's term ends in May. France elects a president in spring 2027, with Marine Le Pen leading polls. Markets barely moved.

items.headline: A trillion-parameter model, free to download
items.gist: Follow-up. Mistral released Mistral Large 4 open weights on Thu 29 Oct, two days before its self-imposed 31 October deadline. About one trillion parameters, multimodal, nicknamed 'Le Chonk'; weights on Hugging Face and the model on Mistral's API. Company claims: comparable to GLM-5.3 while using 47% fewer tokens per task, and top of Artificial Analysis's Coding Agent Index among open models; no published scores in the coverage reached. Positioned for defensive cybersecurity and on-premise deployment across code and IT infrastructure. CEO Arthur Mensch: AI should 'be a tool for empowerment, not dominance.' VP of Science Pierre Stock: access 'that can't be cut off by definition because the model is open-weighted'; he also said the company does not want to 'fearmonger people' about AI security risk. Company line: 'state-of-the-art performance' at 'a fraction of the compute and capital committed by closed labs.' Licence described by several secondary accounts as a modified MIT; the modification could not be confirmed from a primary source and was printed as reported. Thread closed.

items.headline: The best model anyone can buy scores twelve per cent
items.gist: SemiAnalysis published GDPx on 2 Nov, by Max Kan, Andrew Megalaa and Dylan Patel: an agentic benchmark across 11 high-value domains - chip design, cybersecurity, biology, finance, legal, quant trading, recursive self-improvement, hardware design, materials science, alignment, software engineering - deliberately excluding government, real estate and insurance. Tasks built with specialised RL-environment partners in realistic environments (a finance task uses a ~2,000-file deal room); default 8-hour limit; models run in native harnesses or OpenCode; headline score is pass@1 across three attempts, domains and partners equally weighted. Scores: Claude Opus 5.5 12.0% (best overall, leads quant trading, hardware design, chip design), Gemini 4 Carbon 10.9% (best biology, edges software engineering), GPT-6 Astra 9.6% (leads RSI and materials science); Muse Wonder Full best on cyber by a meaningful margin. Safety classifiers depress Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra overall. Finance and legal: essentially every model scores exactly 0 under binary grading, so partial credit is reported for those two; the authors say strong models misjudge authoritative sources and miss second-order implications. They argue GDPval and similar general benchmarks lack realistic environments and often have flawed graders.

items.headline: Apple will ship Chinese AI on a Chinese model
items.gist: Alibaba announced on social media on 1 Nov, agreement struck 31 Oct, that Qwen will power Apple Intelligence in China - Apple's first partnership with a local model developer since Apple Intelligence was cleared for the Chinese market. Chinese users can call Qwen within Siri, writing tools and visual intelligence, drawing on text and image comprehension and content generation. Testable in the latest iOS developer beta from 4 Nov; public launch with iOS 27.3 in December. Qwen is opt-in; Alibaba says user queries and generated responses will not be used to train its models. Eligibility: an Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone bought in China, or device location and Apple Account country both set to China. The Cyberspace Administration of China added Apple Intelligence to its approved list in July 2026. Alibaba CEO Wu Yongming: Qwen 'will be deeply woven into a range of experiences across the Apple ecosystem.' Wang Xiaojie of Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications told Xinhua it is the first time a leading consumer hardware maker has built its Chinese-market AI on a domestically developed large model. No Apple statement; the Korean-language source was machine-translated, so quote wording may differ.

editions.title: Signal — 5 November
editions.lede: A barrel of Brent crude cost $117.64 on Friday. By Wednesday night it cost $93.52.
sections: Set for a price that moved

items.headline: Twenty-four dollars came off a barrel in three days
items.gist: Follow-up to 29 Oct. Brent settled $117.64 Fri 30 Oct, $103.60 Tue 3 Nov, then $93.52 Wed 4 Nov, -$10.08 and -9.73% in the session and about -20% over three sessions; WTI -8.88% to $87.56 on 4 Nov. Early Thu 5 Nov Brent about $93.63, WTI about $87.13. Gasoline futures 17% below Friday's peak; FinanceFeeds put Wednesday's gasoline futures fall at 7.27%. Sources conflict on Friday's base ($117.64 settle per Substack, about $118 peak per Gulf News, about $113 per FinanceFeeds) and on Wednesday's percentage (-9.73% Jan-2027 contract, -9.36% front-month via Oilprice, 'nearly 8%' per Gulf News). Cause disputed: Gulf News credits the Democratic sweep, Vance, Qatari mediation and Trump saying no immediate strike; FinanceFeeds calls the midterms a second-order factor and quotes Phillip Nova's Priyanka Sachdeva on profit-taking and reduced speculative longs. Statements: Vance 2 Nov 'certainly made some progress'; Trump to the FT on election night, no immediate plans to attack; Trump 4 Nov on the war costing votes 'because it drove the gasoline up a little bit short term' and 'if I had it to do again, I'd have to do it again'; US officials told Axios on 5 Nov the military is finishing preparations for possible major combat, not an order. Iran unmoved: a senior security council secretary said 3 Nov the US answer to its seven conditions was 'not satisfactory'; conditions are end of the naval blockade, sanctions relief and release of frozen funds, with one official saying the strait could reopen within two days of that. Qatari draft could restart direct talks within days on a three-day sequence of confidence-building steps. IRGC claims (via Reuters, unverified): four tankers on a forbidden southern route struck mines and exploded on 4 Nov; on 5 Nov another tanker hit a mine, a supertanker caught fire and so did an assisting tug. South Korea sending maritime patrol aircraft and an EOD team. Forecasts: Goldman raised December Brent to $105; Rystad says flows unlikely to return to pre-war levels; JPMorgan put October global surplus at 1.4 mb/d from 1.1. US petrol averaged a record $4.24/gal in Q3, diesel $5.56 and $6.28 in election week. Pre-war Brent implied near $72.

items.headline: Congress changed hands, and Wall Street had its best day in eighteen months
items.gist: Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate on 3 Nov 2026 (CBS, NBC projections through 4 Nov); dozens of House races still uncalled at that point. Hakeem Jeffries, who declared for speaker, said Democrats would finish with at least 255 seats, his own forecast not a count; Democrats held 214 going in. Mike Johnson will not stand for minority leader; Scalise and Jordan are running for it. CBS exit polls: Trump approval 38%, 89% of voters called cost of living a major or crucial factor. Market 4 Nov closes: Dow 53,356.12 +1,569.40 (+3.03%), S&P 500 7,688.62 +119.70 (+1.58%), Nasdaq 25,736.51 +364.50 (+1.44%), Russell 2000 2,856.96 (+1.58%); gold +3.38% to $4,073.70; 10-yr yield about 4.89% on the wire, H.15 shows 4.95% for 3 Nov, 4.91% for 2 Nov, effective funds 3.88%. CNN and Motley Fool called it the best post-midterm session in 44 years without naming the comparison year; a TheStreet desk headline called it the best day since April 2025. Energy was the only falling sector. Quotes: Justin Buell (Continuity Group) 'The midterm elections come at the perfect time to rescue the stock market from its bout of AI-driven volatility'; Daniela Hathorn (Capital.com) on a relief rally and that 'a change in congressional control does not necessarily translate into an immediate change in economic policy'. Kpler's Michelle Brouhard noted the new Congress is not seated until 3 January, and cannot lift the blockade or sanctions in any case. Musk spent a record $474m on the midterms; Tesla -4.91% to $378.93 and SpaceX -5.23% to $133.92 premarket. Trump Media fell sharply; accounts range from -11% to -24.54% so no figure printed.

items.headline: Australia raised rates the day before oil broke
items.gist: RBA raised the cash rate target 25bp to 4.85% on 3 Nov 2026, effective 4 Nov, highest since 2008 and an 18-year high. Vote 6-3: six to raise, three to hold at 4.60%. Fifth rise of 2026; cycle began in February. Statement: 'Inflation remains elevated and recent data indicate that it is broadly based'; 'The inflation outlook has also been revised materially higher'; inflation not expected to reach the top of the 2-3% band until late 2027 and to stay above 3% for the coming year; 'The economy is slowing, housing prices have fallen significantly and the unemployment rate has risen'; unemployment projected to rise by more than the August forecasts; business investment including data centres forecast stronger near term. The explicit tightening bias was dropped, which UBS called 'clearly dovish'; UBS expects a hold. Headline CPI 4.3% y/y for September (next CPI 25 Nov); end-2026 forecast revised to 4.5% from 3.6%; wages 3.4% against prices 3.7% this financial year. Bullock quotes: 'Inflation is too high, and our forecasts suggest it will stay higher for longer'; 'I want to be very clear that we are not tightening monetary policy because of the direct impact of oil prices on inflation'; 'We are not looking to tip the economy into recession if we can avoid it'; 'I don't know what the next move will be'. ASX 200 closed +0.3%; AUD eased to about 69.76 US cents, USD 0.6972 at 4pm 4 Nov. Betashares' David Bassanese expects a February 2027 rise; NAB sees this as the last; Capital Economics expects cuts late next year. Next meeting 8 December.

items.headline: Europe is back to four per cent, and one line explains it
items.gist: Eurostat flash estimate published 4 Nov 2026: euro-area annual inflation 4.0% in October, up from 3.8% in September, highest since September 2023 and a three-year high. Components (annual rates): energy 20.8% (from 18.9%), services 3.3% (from 3.2%), food 1.6% (from 1.3%), other goods 1.2%. Core and non-energy industrial goods not in the accounts reached. Country: Belgium 5.2% per Eurostat against Statbel's own 5.26% the week before, a methodology difference. Contributions are not published with the flash; September's final figures had energy adding 1.71pp of a 3.8% headline with energy about a tenth of the basket. Jack Allen-Reynolds (Capital Economics) says the indirect effect of energy on food prices has remained very limited but could become more visible if energy holds near current levels. ECB held the deposit rate at 2.5% on 29 Oct, markets price a December rise and up to three more by end-2027 to 3.25%. The edition's point: the ECB is setting rates for a year in which its biggest inflation driver has just fallen about a fifth in three sessions.

items.headline: Beijing has made its emergency loans permanent
items.gist: PBOC statement Mon 2 Nov 2026 after meeting the NFRA and CSRC: more use of the Securities, Funds and Insurance companies Swap Facility (SFISF, created Oct 2024) and of the relending facility for share buybacks and shareholding increases. The relending facility becomes a permanent arrangement rather than temporary, with its rate cut from 1.25% to 1%. PBOC also plans more frequent operations, more participating institutions, lower swap fees and optimised collateral. Third SFISF operation Tue 3 Nov, one-year term extendable; 31 securities and fund firms applied for more than 100bn yuan (about US$14.89bn), against 105bn yuan total across the first two operations (Oct 2024 and Jan 2025); no allotment disclosed. Buyback relending: about 440bn yuan of signed agreements, more than 280bn disbursed. CSRC: in the first 10 months of 2026, 645 listed companies disclosed 700 buyback plans totalling 237.7bn yuan, both records; it is also reviewing price-support buyback rules. Unnamed CSRC official: 'Stock repurchase is an important tool for listed companies to manage their market value, and a key means to stabilize stock prices and convey development prospects and confidence.' Trigger: CSI 300 -8.5% in October and down about 15% over a 12-week losing streak, described as its longest on record; STAR 50 down about 40% from its late-June peak, roughly $480bn of value; CSI Semiconductor Index -56% over 84 trading days from a 1 July high to a 3 Nov low. Shanghai Composite +1.1% on 2 Nov, then CSI 300 and Shanghai each about -1% in early trade on 3 Nov. Rebound Wed 4 Nov: STAR Composite +9.90%, ChiNext +6.40%, Shanghai Composite +2.16%, SW Electronics +10.91%, turnover CNY2.05tn (up more than CNY330bn); ChinaAMC STAR Semiconductor ETF limit-up at 20%, Harvest STAR Chip +13.53%, ChinaAMC STAR 50 ETF +10.29%. Fund houses cautious: Guolian An calls it the first volume-backed rebound from a bottoming zone with right-side signals not fully confirmed; China Europe Fund says a reversal needs new capital and better earnings expectations and that a day above 9% may have front-loaded short-term upside; Caitong says policy bottom to market bottom still needs confirmation. Nomura (4 Nov) frames AI capex and negative free cash flow as a timing gap rather than a profitability problem. Caixin, not the regulator, characterised the declines as weighing on the broader economic recovery.

items.headline: Apple's new chief executive has a memory problem
items.gist: Apple fiscal Q4 2026 (quarter ended 26 Sep 2026), reported 2 Nov, first results call hosted by CEO John Ternus, who replaced Tim Cook on 1 September 2026. Revenue $114.5bn +12%, a September-quarter record; diluted EPS $2.10 +14%, including about $0.05 from tariff refunds; gross margin 47.9%, including about 1pp from tariff refunds; operating cash flow $28bn and $28bn returned to shareholders; FY2026 revenue a record $479bn. Segments: iPhone $57.6bn +17% (September-quarter record); Mac $10.8bn from $8.7bn; iPad $6.2bn from $7.0bn (supply constraints and a hard A16 comparison); Wearables, Home and Accessories $8.3bn -8%; Services $31.6bn from $28.8bn, an all-time record (FY $123.3bn). Greater China revenue +21%, a quarterly record. More than 2.5bn active devices. Dividend $0.27, payable 16 Nov to holders of record 12 Nov. December-quarter guidance: revenue growth 7-10% (expected best December ever), Services growth 8-9%, gross margin 45-46%, pressured by higher memory costs and the Siri AI ramp; Mac and iPad constrained mainly by memory. Ternus called the memory situation 'unprecedented' and expects higher memory costs in the December quarter and beyond; June and September price rises offset some of it. COO Sabih Khan said iPhone, iPad and Mac were supply-constrained, partly by advanced-node SoC availability, easing as the line moves to 2nm. CFO Kevan Parekh: 'very early days' on the on-device versus Private Cloud Compute mix and inference costs. Ternus reiterated plans for usage limits on server-side AI features with paid expanded access, no pricing given, and acknowledged display issues on iPhone Duo with a 'very small percentage' returned. Context printed: SK hynix 80% and Samsung 55% operating margins on memory last quarter.

items.headline: The memory bill reaches the phone makers
items.gist: Qualcomm fiscal Q4 2026 (quarter ended 27 Sep 2026), reported 4 Nov: GAAP revenue $10,322m -8% (non-GAAP $10,442m, GAAP excludes a $120m customer payment from a legal settlement); non-GAAP EBT $2,666m -30%; GAAP diluted EPS $1.17, non-GAAP $2.17 -28%. QCT revenue $9,015m -8%, EBT $2,142m -26% on a 24% margin; handsets $5,137m -26%, automotive $1,990m +89%, IoT $1,888m +4%. QTL revenue $1,304m -7%, EBT $918m -10% on a 70% margin. FY2026: GAAP revenue $43,120m -3%, GAAP EPS $12.70 (including a $5.7bn tax benefit worth $5.32), non-GAAP EPS $10.54 -12%; handsets $24,072m -13%, automotive $6,004m +52%, IoT $7,132m +8%. Fiscal Q1 2027 guidance: revenue $10.4-11.2bn, QCT $9.0-9.6bn inclusive of Data Center, QTL $1.3-1.5bn, GAAP EPS $1.03-1.23, non-GAAP $2.15-2.35; input-cost pricing actions fully in QCT gross margins in H2 FY2027. FY26 capital returns $11,671m ($7,817m buybacks, $3,854m dividends). CEO Cristiano Amon: 'Fiscal 2027 marks the start of our non-handset revenue inflection, including the ramp of our Data Center business'; non-handset revenue projected to grow more than 60% y/y; FY2027 Data Center revenue target reiterated at $5bn; multi-generational product collaboration with Amazon announced; QTL licences renewed with Apple, Huawei and Transsion. Shares fell more than 9% in extended trade. Arm fiscal Q2 2027 (quarter ended 30 Sep 2026), same afternoon: revenue a record $1.443bn +27%, above a $1.38bn guidance midpoint; licensing $773m +50%, about $100m above expectations per CFO Jason Child; royalties $670m +8%, below expectations; ACV $1.79bn +12%; GAAP net income $130m -45% and GAAP EPS $0.12 against $0.22, dragged by a $46.6m fair-value loss on equities, a $4.9m Arm China credit loss and a prior-year $131m Artisan sale gain; non-GAAP net income $566m +36% and EPS $0.52 +33%; GAAP operating margin 13.9%; operating cash flow $207m -63%. Q3 guidance revenue $1.54bn +/-$50m, non-GAAP EPS $0.56 +/-$0.04, licensing growth slightly above 50%, royalties up low single digits y/y. Arm AGI CPU, its first in-house data-centre processor co-designed with Meta and launched March 2026, demand raised from about $1bn to more than $2bn across FY2027-28, first commercial deliveries expected in fiscal Q4 2027; data-centre royalties doubled y/y. Child named memory price rises as hurting low- and mid-range smartphone shipments. Arm shares fell about 4-5% after hours. Asian chipmakers on Thu 5 Nov: SK hynix -7.4%, Samsung Electronics -5.7%, Advantest more than -11%, Lasertec -12.5%, Kioxia -9.2% on its own guidance; Chinese semiconductor shares mostly higher on Beijing's support measures.

items.headline: Marvell bought a laser company for $115bn, and both shares fell
items.gist: Merger agreement signed Sun 1 Nov 2026, announced 2 Nov, unanimously approved by both boards: Marvell Technology acquires Lumentum all-stock at a fixed 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share, with cash for fractions. Enterprise value put at $115bn by the companies, equivalent to $1,132 per Lumentum share at 28 October closes, a 23.9% premium to Lumentum's $913.95 close that day. Ownership: Marvell holders about 67%, Lumentum holders about 33%. Matt Murphy stays chairman and CEO; three Lumentum directors including CEO Michael Hurlston join a seven-member board. Expected close first half of 2028; outside date 1 Nov 2027 extendable in three-month steps to 1 Aug 2028 if only regulatory approvals remain. Approvals: both shareholder votes, Hart-Scott-Rodino, Form S-4 effectiveness, Nasdaq listing. Break fees: Marvell pays $3.2bn on a regulatory failure and $5.8bn in other cases; Lumentum pays $2.9bn. Rationale: Murphy, 'AI infrastructure is undergoing a fundamental architectural shift toward optical connectivity'; the release argues copper is reaching its physical limits. Lumentum makes high-power and pump lasers, optical circuit switches and optical transceivers, with its own indium phosphide compound-semiconductor fabs; mostly 800G cloud transceivers with 1.6T ramping, and external laser sources for near- and co-packaged optics. Combined addressable market put at $550bn by 2030; synergies more than $1bn a year; accretive to Marvell's adjusted EPS in year one. Share reaction 2 Nov 09:44 ET: Marvell $186.38 -5.1% from $196.40, Lumentum $765.52 -8.9% from $840.70; Marvell had already fallen about 22% from $251.65 on 28 Oct to $196.40 on 30 Oct before signing. Lumentum fiscal Q1 2027 (quarter to 26 Sep 2026): revenue $1.26bn +136.5%, net income $360.3m, non-GAAP EPS $4.57 against a $4.05-4.35 forecast; fiscal Q2 guidance revenue $1.575-1.625bn and EPS $5.90-6.20; Hurlston cited purchase commitments exceeding $5bn. No source established a formal semiconductor M&A record, so none was claimed.

items.headline: A tampered installer in June, a fake job offer in September
items.gist: Follow-up to 2 November. Binance posted an initial incident report on X on Tue 3 Nov 2026 giving a root cause for the 29 Oct theft of about $6.34bn. Chain: in June a Wallet DevOps engineer was compromised through a tampered Homebrew installation; in September a second employee was targeted via a fraudulent recruitment process and a malicious coding assignment; on 20 Oct the attackers used that employee's computer and an internal AI tool to reach two other engineers' devices and found a container deployment permission; on 29 Oct, nine days later, they deployed a container and ran a malicious script that launched the wallet attack. Binance says it has closed the entry points, rebuilt or replaced affected systems and commissioned an independent cybersecurity review, which has not reported. Recovery claims, all Binance's own and unverified independently: 90% replenished by 31 Oct, about 95% by 2 Nov, 98% of impacted assets by 3 Nov, with about $2.85bn frozen or intercepted. Wikipedia's unsourced tally has about $3bn frozen by issuers, $1.5bn unfreezable and about $1.8bn still with the attackers. Withdrawals reopened in phases from 04:00 UTC on 3 Nov across BSC, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, Sui, Arbitrum, Optimism, TRON and Base, after a first reopening on 1 Nov; no source says the full asset list is restored. A zero-knowledge proof-of-reserves snapshot covering BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD and ZEC was completed 2 Nov; co-CEO Yi He said the full proof needs about 40-50 hours of computation after the snapshot, and another snapshot was planned for 4 Nov with no reported result. Co-CEO Richard Teng: 'There's still work to do.' FBI Cyber alert 31 Oct linked the theft to North Korea and published ETH, BTC and SOL addresses; the US Secret Service is tracking funds; TRM Labs and onchain investigators attribute it to TraderTraitor. On 2 Nov Kim Jong-un's sister called the FBI claims a 'grave political provocation'. SomaXBT claimed on 1 Nov that about $242m was laundered on Tron, unverified. Bitcoin +3.5% to about $80,500 on 4 Nov; ether +6% to $2,433. No sanctions, charges or formal regulatory action reported.

items.headline: WordPress leaves a door open while it updates itself
items.gist: CVE-2026-119977, a time-of-check/time-of-use race condition in WordPress core's full-upgrade process, CVSS 8.1. During a full core upgrade WordPress extracts the package into a staging directory under wp-content/upgrade; on affected setups those files are web-reachable while the update runs and briefly expose a standalone copy of the WordPress installer, which an attacker can point at a database they control, giving a path to server code execution. No account and no user interaction needed, but precise timing during an upgrade is required. Affected: WordPress 4.7 through 7.1.3; fixed in 7.1.4, released 28 October 2026; backports for eligible older branches reported but not confirmed. Reported by Umut Bayram. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 3 November 2026 with a federal remediation deadline of 6 November, reported via Security Affairs and Elets and not checked against CISA's own alert. CISA confirms exploitation but names no attacker and no victim count. Wordfence recorded its first firewall-rule hit nine minutes after the rule went live and more than 18,500 requests aimed at staged installer paths in 21 hours; other tallies are 12,632 blocked attacks in a day (Elets) and 60,471 blocked attempts in 24 hours; a Previdian honeypot logged three attempts on 30 Oct from a UK address. All are attempts, not confirmed compromises, and no figure for compromised sites has been published. Automatic updates do not protect by themselves and are what create the window; advice is to confirm in Dashboard > Updates that 7.1.4 installed and to block public access to wp-content/upgrade until then. No share-of-the-web figure given in the sources used.
